profile.reading:
This facility is operated by Dynamics Mining, a cryptocurrency mining hosting company, in Hopkins County, Kentucky. The prior record for this facility carried no operator name; this registry corrects that gap directly and also flags this as a distinct category from the traditional colocation, cloud, or wholesale data centers tracked elsewhere in this registry: it hosts Bitcoin mining hardware on behalf of clients rather than providing general-purpose enterprise IT infrastructure or colocation cabinets.

Per its own site, Dynamics Mining sells Bitcoin mining hardware and offers hosting services for client-owned mining rigs, and states it has built and operated more than five such facilities over roughly three years across Maine, Colorado, Georgia, Tennessee, and Kentucky. This Hopkins County, Kentucky site is one of that multi-state footprint, though this registry has not independently confirmed which of Dynamics Mining's facilities specifically corresponds to this address beyond the county-level location match.

Cryptocurrency mining facilities differ structurally from traditional data centers: they optimize for cheap, often stranded or curtailed electricity and high-density, purpose-built compute racks running mining hardware (ASICs) rather than general enterprise servers, and typically do not publish IT capacity in the same terms (technical square footage, redundant Tier-rated power) that colocation and cloud operators use. No megawatt capacity, square footage, or year-opened date specific to this Kentucky site was found in sourcing available this session; Dynamics Mining's public materials describe its footprint at the company level rather than per-site.

reading.body:
This facility is operated by Dynamics Mining, a cryptocurrency mining hosting company, and is located in Hopkins County, Kentucky. The operator markets Bitcoin mining hardware and hosting services for client-owned mining rigs, and states it has built and operated more than five such facilities across Maine, Colorado, Georgia, Tennessee, and Kentucky over roughly three years. No megawatt capacity, square footage, or opening date specific to this Kentucky site has been published.

Cryptocurrency mining facilities differ structurally from traditional data centers. They optimize for cheap or curtailed electricity and high-density racks running purpose-built mining hardware, or ASICs, rather than general enterprise servers. Operators in this category typically do not publish IT capacity in the same terms as colocation and cloud operators, making power consumption and compute density difficult to assess from available public materials.

Kentucky has five mapped data center facilities on record, of which three have published power specifications totaling 9.55 megawatts. This facility does not publish a megawatt figure and cannot be ranked against other Kentucky sites by capacity. Whether this campus matters to AI scaling depends on its actual power draw and hardware composition, neither of which the operator has disclosed.
